From the politicians perspective, addressing the topic of drugs can be a daunting and difficult endeavor. There is a great deal of risk involved, with little reward to be gained. Suggesting policy changes that make ‘narcotics’ more available can make a politician susceptible to character assassination through biased media sources, and it will inevitably cost him or her the votes of those who categorically dismiss the idea of ending ‘the war of drugs’ (usually through fear, or a generally close-minded attitude toward drugs). As a consequence, the people cannot rely upon politicians to engage with this topic on their own; the debate must be forced onto their agenda through popular demand.

How can you create pressure, forcing drug policy onto a platform for discussion ahead of elections? My suggestion is simple. Whenever someone engages you in a conversation related to voting/elections, be it a representative of some political party that shows up on your doorstep, or friends, or family; simply tell them that you have decided not to vote for anyone, unless they commit to do X about the current policy on narcotic substances in your country/state. I understand that saying something like this may be difficult depending on who you are talking to. It’s easier to say this to a close friend, or a complete stranger, than it is to tell your colleagues, your boss, or your ultra-conservative grandmother. Adjust your message to fit the audience. Nevertheless, make it clear that you will not vote for a party or candidate that will not commit to drug reform, regardless of their stance in other policy areas.

You have one vote to contribute. You are one voice among many; your vote will ultimately make little to no difference. The point here is that recruiters, other people, politicians, and the leaders of political parties will hear about your decision. If you truly desire drug reform, then signal that this is your stance as often as you can.

Recruiters feed information upward to those who propose policy. Candidates and parties spend money to learn where the people stand on different issues through surveys and other means of communicating with the masses. Whenever you get a change to speak into these lines of communication; tell them your stance on drug policy, and tell them that meeting your demands is essential for your support. Do not make it about weighing the candidate/party’s stance on drugs up against their stance on other (albeit important) issues like taxation, immigration, welfare, etc. Tell them, clearly, that their stance on any other policy area is completely irrelevant if they do not commit to drug policy reform. Tell that that you would rather ‘waste’ your vote on an underdog, or not vote at all, unless the party/candidate you favor will adhere to your demands.

I promised I would not get into a discussion about the why drug policy must change, but please understand that I do not seek to undermine the importance of other policy areas. If you wish publicly advocate the stance outlined above, please ensure that you do not neglect to understand and discuss other areas of policy. Don’t go out into the world and say ‘I don’t care about taxation, all that matters to me is drug reform’. The other policy areas still matter, and you should still engage with them. The point is to make it clear, or at least make it seem like drug policy reform is pivotal for your vote; the only policy area that can make or break your support.
